Reduced restraint of the experimentally catagen-promoting TGF-beta2 signal could favor premature catagen. Both the loss of restraint and the resulting timing defect remain untested in APMR1.
Premature regression could contribute to hair loss if the candidate mechanism operates in APMR1. The congenital phenotype could instead involve follicle formation or another fetuin-A function.

nodes.description: Homozygous AHSG c.950G>A (p.Arg317His) was reported in seven affected members of one consanguineous Iranian family. AHSG lies within the independently mapped APMR1 interval. The clinical association is supported by segregation, positional evidence and altered protein migration, but the direction of protein dysfunction and tissue mechanisms are unresolved.

nodes.description: Intellectual disability was described as severe in the original Pakistani linkage family. The AHSG-associated family had variable intellectual disability; the 2021 review summarizes IQ values of 40–54 for its seven relatives. These ascertained families do not establish population frequencies or a uniform severity, and molecular equivalence of the linkage family remains unproven.

nodes.description: Homozygous missense variant reported with APMR1. The original report called it predicted pathogenic. The LIKELY_PATHOGENIC value here records the ClinVar RCV000578120.9 aggregate classification, last evaluated March 24, 2026, rather than a new curator ACMG classification. The record has two submissions but criteria from one submitter; this is not evidence of two independently phenotyped APMR1 families. Protein migration is altered, while the functional direction remains unresolved.

nodes.description: Reduced antagonism of TGF-beta ligands is a proposed consequence of the APMR1 allele. Normal fetuin binds TGF-beta/BMP ligands in vitro, but deficient binding or neutralization has not been demonstrated for p.Arg317His. This node is conditional on the stated hypothesis.
